subject: Clarification: Third‑party roster + data residency guarantees for GlobalPay
messages:
From: GlobalPay Security <security@globalpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: current subprocessor roster + residency assurances

Hi Jordan,

Quick request from our security and procurement teams — we are finalizing our vendor approval for Redwood and need an up-to-date third‑party processor roster, including:
- the processor name and role (e.g., logging, analytics, CDN, KMS)
- country(ies) where Customer Data may be processed or routed
- whether any of the processors are located outside the US/EU (and if so, mitigation controls)
- whether any temporary cross‑border access or vendor changes are planned within the next 90 days

Also, please confirm whether Redwood can commit to data residency for our tenant in the US region (i.e., no customer data egress to non‑US processors without prior notice). A short paragraph referencing your DPA clauses would be helpful.

Can you get this to us by EOD Thursday?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
GlobalPay Security
security@globalpay.com

Adding the roster and a proposed legal paragraph — draft below. I also flagged the three processors that warrant an explicit note (EdgeBridge CDN, LogFlow analytics, KeySafe KMS SLA partner).

Proposed DPA paragraph (draft):
"Redwood Inference maintains an up‑to‑date list of subprocessors as required under Section 4.2 of the DPA. For customers with a US data residency requirement, Redwood will ensure that Customer Data is stored and processed within US data centers and will not transfer Customer Data to subprocessors located outside the United States without prior written notice and a documented mitigation plan. For subprocessors that may process transient metadata or provide caching/edge functionality outside the US, Redwood enforces contractual restrictions, encryption at rest and in transit, and contractual obligations equivalent to those in our DPA (including SCCs where applicable)."

Planned changes: we do have a short window in ~45 days where EdgeBridge is scheduled for capacity expansion in APAC; that work is strictly for cached responses and metadata; we will provide advance notice to affected customers and offer options to opt out or pin to specific regions for enterprise plans.

Attachments included: subprocessor_roster_20290611.xlsx, proposed-response-GlobalPay.docx

Let me know if you want me to send directly to GlobalPay or you want to send on behalf of Sales.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Hi Alex — attaching the canonical subprocessor roster and a short paragraph from our privacy team that references the DPA. See key points below:

- Attached: subprocessor_roster_20290611.xlsx (role + country + contact)
- Residency: For US‑region tenants Redwood stores and processes customer content in US data centers by default and will not direct Customer Data to non‑US subprocessors without prior written notice, per Section 4.2 of our DPA.
- Exceptions: transient metadata or caching at the edge may be processed outside the US for performance (EdgeBridge CDN); we enforce encryption, contractual restrictions, and will provide advance notice for any planned APAC expansion (planned ~45 days out).

Next steps: if procurement needs a signed addendum or any additional attestations we can route to Legal for a quick DocuSign. Linking the roster here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/subprocessor_roster_20290611 and a draft addendum if needed.
